clue.text: Parrot primarily mimicking a cry of another bird

indicators.note: primarily asks for the leading letter of the word mimicking, its first and primary part

parts.note: a caw is the harsh call of a crow or rook

explanation.surface: A parrot is mostly heard copying the call of some other bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The macaw is a large, brightly coloured tropical American parrot.

clue.text: Mean person holding test, judge of what's right and wrong

definitions.text: judge of what's right and wrong

indicators.note: holding means the stingy person's word contains the other piece

parts.note: a miser is a mean, stingy person
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A stingy examiner sets himself up as an arbiter of ethics.
explanation.definitionFit: A moraliser pronounces on the ethics of others, judging right from wrong.

clue.text: Lid covering fowl fattened for pot

parts.note: a cap is a lid or top
on means covering, lying on top of

explanation.surface: A lid goes over a bird plumped up for the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table.

clue.text: Scottish fibs about king seen in some publications

indicators.note: about means the Scottish phrase goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: wee is Scots for small, so wee lies are little fibs
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Untruths about a monarch appear in the Scottish press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scottish' signals the Scots word for small, so the fibs are little ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeklies are magazines or papers issued once a week, a class of publications.

clue.text: In one's youth, crossing one Eastern region

indicators.note: crossing means the phrase straddles the other piece, so it is placed within it

parts.note: in one's youth means while one was still under age, as a minor
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone recalls travelling through an Eastern land when young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts I (one) inside AS A MINOR, the phrase meaning 'in one's youth'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anatolian peninsula, the western end of Asia, is historically called by this name: a region east of Europe.

clue.text: Once more, a legless type wastes time

indicators.note: wastes means the creature's name loses a letter, which is squandered away

parts.note: legless is slang for drunk, as in the saying pissed as a newt

explanation.surface: Again, a drunk fritters away the hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legless' means drunk, not limbless: the newt of the drunkard's simile. 'wastes' removes T (time) from NEWT.
explanation.definitionFit: Anew means again, once more or afresh.

clue.text: Cow I had accepted by friend

indicators.note: accepted by means the contraction is taken inside the friend's word

parts.note: an intimate is a close friend
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A cow I once owned was welcomed by a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' looks like the animal, but it is the verb, to browbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to frighten them into submission, to intimidate.

clue.text: A voice that comes from the heart

definitions.meaning: Ancient Greek has a grammatical voice between active and passive, named this way
something central, from the very centre or heart of a thing

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests sincere speech, but 'voice' is the grammatical term.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a Greek grammatical voice and also means central, from the heart of something.

clue.text: Bad flaws in feeble report quickly revealed

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters are placed inside the word for feeble

parts.note: nesh is a dialect word for feeble or soft

indicators.note: bad means the letters of flaws are spoilt and come out in a corrupted order

explanation.surface: A weak report has serious faults.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for feeble is a northern English dialect term meaning soft or susceptible to cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsflash is a brief urgent bulletin, news given out at once.

clue.text: Again deposit article in bank

indicators.note: in means the article sits inside the verb for bank

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone puts an item back into the bank once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in 'bank on'; 'in' puts A inside RELY.
explanation.definitionFit: To relay is to lay again, putting something down a second time.

clue.text: Show in theatre to object to

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
to resent something is to take objection to it

explanation.surface: A critic objects to a production staged at the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent something is to depict or show it, as a painting does a scene.

clue.text: Almost shine wooden peg

indicators.note: almost means the phrase falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to shine at something is to do well at it

explanation.surface: A carpenter nearly polishes a peg made of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last letter from DO WELL (shine), leaving DOWEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowel is a headless wooden pin used to join pieces of timber.

clue.text: Solitary Dutch artist holds on

indicators.note: holds means the painter's name wraps round the other piece

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely was a Dutch-born portrait painter at the English court

explanation.surface: A lonely Dutch painter keeps going at his work.
explanation.walkthrough: Lely painted the court beauties of Charles II; 'Dutch artist' in crosswords is often him.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary and lonely both describe someone alone, without company.

clue.text: Young ones in school, people of little importance

definitions.meaning: fry are young fish, and fish swim in schools; children at school are also called this

explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is the fishing sense, a shoal, as well as the classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means young fish or children, and by extension unimportant people.

clue.text: The French back secures a try, without committing offence

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)

indicators.note: secures means the rugby player holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: in rugby the wings are among the backs
a bid is an attempt or try

explanation.surface: A French rugby back scores a try cleanly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' and 'back' suggest rugby scoring, and back is indeed the position: WING, a back, secures A BID (a try).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone law-abiding keeps the law, so acts without committing offences.

clue.text: Workers who adjust scenery as old vehicle passes

parts.note: a stage is a stagecoach, a horse-drawn vehicle of old
to hand something is to pass it over

explanation.surface: Theatre crew shift the set as an antique carriage goes by.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagehands are the backstage crew who move scenery and props.

clue.text: TV presenter, the one running last in 8

definitions.meaning: the main presenter of a television news programme
8 is a relay, and the final, strongest runner of a relay team is called this

explanation.walkthrough: '8' refers to the answer at 8 down, a relay race.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a news presenter and also the final leg runner in a relay team.

clue.text: Academic stream, with pressure on, affected

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the second piece after the first, attached to it

parts.note: the Cam is the river flowing through Cambridge, a university town
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A student pressured at university behaves pretentiously.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'academic stream' is the River Cam at Cambridge; P (pressure) goes 'on' after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp behaviour is exaggerated and theatrical, that is, affected.

clue.text: Breaking payroll up in way many people like

indicators.note: breaking means the words are broken up and reassembled in a different order

explanation.surface: Breaking up the payroll is a widely liked move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' rearranges PAYROLL UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something popularly is to do it in a way that wins wide favour.

clue.text: Enthusiasm good to see in act, having eliminated errors

indicators.note: to see in means the pieces are placed inside the word for act

parts.note: a deed is an act
a bug is a craze or enthusiasm, as in the travel bug

explanation.surface: Keenness is good to witness in a performance free of faults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' as enthusiasm is the sense in 'caught the travel bug'.
explanation.definitionFit: Software that is debugged has had its faults, known as bugs, removed.

clue.text: Blue fish caught inside

indicators.note: inside means the abbreviation sits within the fish's name

parts.note: a ray is a flat cartilaginous fish
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A sad-looking fish ends up hooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' suggests sad or a colour, but here it means risqué; 'inside' puts C (caught) into RAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes are smutty ones, so blue means racy, mildly indecent.

clue.text: Pleb that is mistreated in naval craft

indicators.note: mistreated means the letters are handled roughly and knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A common sailor is bullied aboard a warship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistreated' rearranges the letters of PLEB THAT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A battleship is a heavily armed warship, a kind of naval vessel.

clue.text: Heads or tails, possibly

parts.note: not a coin toss but the tips or sharp ends of things: a headland, or the tapering end of something

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a coin toss, but heads and tails here are tips: a headland is one, so is the tapering end of an object.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland is named this way, as is the tip of a tail or blade: both are sharp ends.

clue.text: Help for witness still partly assembled

parts.note: a still is a photograph, a single frame
to fit parts is to put them together, assembling something piece by piece

explanation.surface: A witness is helped by a picture pieced together from bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' is the noun, a photograph, not the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Police build such a composite face from a witness's description to help identify a suspect.

clue.text: Home of fair maid getting saucy husband finally

indicators.note: finally places the abbreviation at the very end, after the other piece

parts.note: pert means cheeky or saucy

explanation.surface: A pretty young woman lands a cheeky spouse at last.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fair Maid of Perth is a novel by Sir Walter Scott, set in that Scottish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Perth is the home of Scott's heroine, the Fair Maid of Perth.

clue.text: Tropical singer repeating endless nonsense

indicators.note: repeating means the shortened word is given twice in a row
endless means the word for nonsense loses its final letter

parts.note: bull is slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: A tropical performer keeps singing the same rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims BULL (nonsense) to BUL, and 'repeating' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulbul is a songbird of tropical Africa and Asia, so a singer of the tropics.

clue.text: Energy put into strike, as mentioned later

indicators.note: put into means the abbreviation is inserted within the word for strike

parts.note: a blow is a strike or hit
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Power is put into a punch, as noted further on.
explanation.definitionFit: In a document, see below means a point is dealt with further down, mentioned later.

clue.text: Follower of revolutionary or moderate movement

definitions.meaning: a follower of Leon Trotsky, the Russian revolutionary
a horse's gait between walk and canter, or a steady jog

explanation.definitionFit: The word is short for Trotskyist and also names a medium-paced gait.

clue.text: European citizen runs Arab country

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A European national manages a Gulf state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' looks like a verb (manages), but it is R, the cricket scorebook abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Rome, a European city, is called this.

clue.text: Not even one of Sherlock's street kids

definitions.meaning: uneven, not regular in shape or pattern
Sherlock Holmes used a gang of urchins, the Baker Street ..., as informants

explanation.definitionFit: The word means uneven, and also a member of Holmes's band of street urchins.

clue.text: Vision of the future?

parts.note: looks like foresight, but read as the view you will have in the future, looking back on events after they happen

explanation.walkthrough: The obvious reading is foresight; the joke is that clarity about today only comes later, looking back.
explanation.definitionFit: This is wisdom after the event, the clear view one has once things are in the past.

clue.text: Wife in boat bringing present for husband

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation sits inside the boat's name

parts.note: a dory is a small flat-bottomed fishing boat

explanation.surface: A bride arrives by boat carrying a gift for her groom.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowry is property a bride brings to her husband on marriage, a gift to him.
